articles.headline: Russell Westbrook joins board of basketball league Project B
articles.description: Recently retired Russell Westbrook has joined new men's and women's basketball league Project B as a co-founder and chief strategy officer.

images.credit: Photo by Joe Murphy/NBAE via Getty Images

articles.headline: How do the WNBA playoffs work? Dates, format and more
articles.description: The 2026 WNBA playoffs begins on Sept. 27. Learn more about postseason dates, rules, and stats now.

images.name: Paige Bueckers [608x342]
images.caption: Paige Bueckers is leading the Wings to their first playoff berth since 2023.

articles.headline: Wings' Li to miss FIBA World Cup due to lost passport
articles.description: China will have to play without Li Yueru at the women's FIBA World Cup after her replacement passport was lost in the mail ahead of the tournament that starts in Germany this week.

images.name: Li Yueru [600x400]
images.caption: Li Yueru has had a series of strong performances since being traded to the Dallas Wings last month.

articles.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: Team USA analysis, rankings, rosters
articles.description: Sixteen nations will compete in the World Cup in Berlin starting Friday. Team USA and France are front-runners.

images.name: Gabby Williams and Jackie Young [1296x729]
images.caption: Gabby Williams and France nearly toppled Jackie Young and the U.S. women at the Paris Games, losing 67-66 in the gold medal game. Both are back to lead their teams in the World Cup.
images.credit: Damien MEYER / AFP via Getty Images

images.name: Awa Fam [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Awa Fam, right, scored in double figures in three of her last four games for the Seattle Storm.

images.name: Julie Allemand [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Julie Allemand had 12 assists and 11 points for the Toronto Tempo in an Aug. 6 loss.

images.name: Han Xu and Janelle Salaun [1296x729]
images.caption: The 6-foot-11 Han Xu, left, of the New York Liberty adds to China's already formidable frontcourt, while Janelle Salaun, who plays for the Golden State Valkyries, represents France.

categories.description: Ssports FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup

series.description: Ssports FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup

articles.headline: Why are there no WNBA games for two weeks? More about FIBA break
articles.description: League stars will be lacing up their shoes, but it won't be on WNBA courts.

articles.headline: 2026 WNBA championship odds: Lynx still odds-on title favorites; Aces, Valkyries next
articles.description: The Lynx remain odds-on favorites to win the WNBA championship, while the red-hot Valkyries are back up to third on the oddsboard.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier, Olivia Miles and the Lynx are winners of 16 of their past 17 games.
images.alt: Olivia Miles #5 of the Minnesota Lynx reacts to a foul call next to Napheesa Collier #24 during WNBA game against the Golden State Valkyries on August 19, 2026 at Chase Center in San Francisco, CA.

images.name: Napheesa Collier [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier and the Lynx enter the week at even money to win the WNBA championship.
images.alt: Napheesa Collier #24 of the Minnesota Lynx drives to the basket during the game against the Las Vegas Aces on August 15, 2026 at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada.

images.name: Napheesa Collier [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier, Natasha Howard and the Minnesota Lynx continue to roll.
images.alt: Napheesa Collier #24 of the Minnesota Lynx celebrates with teammate Natasha Howard #1 against the Toronto Tempo during the second half at Scotiabank Arena on July 30, 2026 in Toronto, Canada.

images.name: Napheesa Collier [1296x729]
images.caption: Napheesa Collier's welcome return only boosts a Lynx team that's the current favorite to win the WNBA Finals.
images.alt: Napheesa Collier #24 of the Minnesota Lynx shoots a free throw during the game against the Seattle Storm on July 22, 2026 at Climate Pledge Arena in Seattle, Washington.

images.name: Olivia Miles for Odds File (260720) [1296x729]
images.caption: Rookie of the Year front-runner Olivia Miles is one of the big reasons that the sportsbooks have made the Minnesota Lynx the team to beat for the championship this season.
images.alt: Olivia Miles #5 of the Minnesota Lynx looks on during the game against the Portland Fire on July 18, 2026 at Target Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

images.name: Gabby Williams  [1296x729]
images.caption: Gabby Williams leads the Valkyries in scoring with 15.0 PPG.
images.alt: Gabby Williams #1 of the Golden State Valkyries dribbles the ball during the game =a  on July 6, 2026 at  CareFirst Arena in Washington, D.C.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: Olivia Miles and the Minnesota Lynx are now alone in front as favorites to win the WNBA championship.
images.alt: Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles (5) dribbles past Dallas Wings guard Azzi Fudd (35) during the WNBA game between the Dallas Wings and the Minnesota Lynx on June 28, 2026, at College Park Center in Arlington, TX.

images.name: Natasha Howard of Minnesota Lynx [608x342]
images.caption: A strong start to the season has the Lynx tied with the Aces for the shortest title odds, just ahead of the Liberty.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: The Lynx have seen their odds shorten but have a tough schedule this week.
images.alt: Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles (5) drives past Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers during the second half of a WNBA basketball game in Arlington, Texas, Thursday, May 14, 2026.

images.name: Olivia Miles [1296x729]
images.caption: Rookie of the Year favorite Olivia Miles is helping drive the early success of the Minnesota Lynx.

images.name: Paige Bueckers [1296x729]
images.caption: Paige Bueckers and her 19.3 PPG is a big reason for the encouraging start by the Wings.
